root_cause.text: In the qat_6xxx driver's probe function, when `adf_dev_up()` partially completes and fails, the IRQ handlers registered during its call are not freed before devres cleanup releases the MSI-X vectors, because `adf_dev_down()` is not called on this error path, leading to a use-after-free of the interrupt handler entries.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "When adf_dev_up() partially completes and then fails, the IRQ handlers registered during adf_isr_resource_alloc() are not detached before the MSI-X vectors are released." The patch adds `adf_dev_down(accel_dev)` in the error path of `adf_dev_up()` to properly free IRQ handlers before devres tears down the vectors.

intent_record.how: On failure of adf_dev_up, the function now performs cleanup by calling adf_dev_down to undo any partial initialization, ensuring proper device state before propagating the error.

candidates.rationale: This condition checks the return value of adf_dev_up, but on failure it directs to an early return without calling adf_dev_down, leaving IRQ handlers unfreed before devres cleanup.
This early return on adf_dev_up failure bypasses any cleanup (including adf_dev_down), causing IRQ handlers to remain registered and leading to use-after-free when MSI-X vectors are released.
